docker_compose_file:
# The redaction witness, as a dstack application.
#
# THIS FILE IS MEASURED. dstack hashes app-compose.json -- which embeds this
# file verbatim -- into MRCONFIGID. Every value below, including the redaction
# mode and the body bound, is therefore part of the enclave's identity: an
# operator cannot change one without changing the measurement, and a client
# pinning the measurement will refuse the changed deployment until it is
# re-allowlisted. That is the intended property, not a side effect.
#
# After editing, regenerate app-compose.json:
#
#     ./build-app-compose.sh
#
# A change here that is not carried into app-compose.json deploys the OLD
# configuration. The script is how the two are kept from drifting.

services:
  witness:
    # By digest, never a tag: a tag is a moving target and a measurement
    # pinned over one is pinning nothing.
    #
    # Built by the `witness-image` workflow from commit f8d3a95 -- natively
    # amd64, because TDX is Intel, and in CI rather than on a developer
    # machine because this image is not reproducibly buildable. A measurement
    # therefore pins a specific artifact only its builder can produce, which
    # makes who built it part of what an auditor is trusting; a public run log
    # answers that better than a laptop.
    #
    # Replacing this means rebuilding and re-pinning the measurement
    # everywhere it is named -- in ingest and in every client.
    image: ghcr.io/tracecommons/trace-commons-witness@sha256:389b9198a4d20b39009963a85c74c68d86bd8a42d7b8ebfbca06199b526c8dd0

    # A restart re-derives the same signing key: dstack's KMS derives the app
    # key from the app id, which does not move. So a restart is invisible to a
    # client that has pinned the signing address, and the witness holds no
    # state that a restart could lose.
    restart: always

    # The witness writes nothing. A writable root filesystem would be a place
    # for a raw transcript to land.
    read_only: true
    tmpfs:
      - /tmp:rw,noexec,nosuid,size=16m

    cap_drop:
      - ALL
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true

    # The guest agent's unix socket. This is the only mount, and it is what
    # GetKey and GetQuote are reached through. It is not network-reachable;
    # the witness proxies GetQuote on /v1/attestation precisely because a
    # contributor cannot call it directly.
    volumes:
      - /var/run/dstack.sock:/var/run/dstack.sock

    environment:
      # 0.0.0.0, not the binary's 127.0.0.1 default. The default is correct for
      # a host where something else terminates TLS in the same netns; inside a
      # container it makes the witness unreachable from dstack-gateway, and the
      # symptom is a healthy-looking process that no request ever arrives at.
      TRACE_COMMONS_WITNESS_BIND: "0.0.0.0:8088"

      # `deterministic-only` or `full-pipeline`, and the binary refuses to start
      # if it is neither -- there is no default in either direction.
      #
      # This deployment runs `full-pipeline`: the deterministic pass, then the
      # prose-PII classifier over its output, which is the same two stages in
      # the same order that ingest applies. A `deterministic-only` certificate
      # carries the deterministic policy alias, and the server's policy
      # allowlist is what keeps such a certificate from admitting a trace no
      # classifier ever read -- so the mode here decides whether these
      # certificates can lift the PII backstop hold at all.
      TRACE_COMMONS_WITNESS_REDACTION: "full-pipeline"

      # The classifier, resolved at startup: a witness told to run
      # `full-pipeline` with no usable backend does not bind, and a backend
      # that fails mid-request refuses rather than degrading to the
      # deterministic result.
      #
      # THIS IS A TRUST-BOUNDARY DECISION, taken deliberately. `near-ai` is an
      # endpoint OUTSIDE this enclave, so partially-redacted text leaves the
      # CVM. The deterministic pass has already run, so credentials and local
      # paths are masked in what goes out -- that ordering is why it is this
      # way round -- but prose PII is still present in it. Choosing this backend
      # places the classifier's operator inside the trust boundary of every
      # transcript this witness sees. The alternative, a sibling classifier
      # container inside the CVM, leaks nothing and costs a multi-gigabyte
      # model on CVM vCPUs at roughly 58 characters per second.
      TRACE_PRIVACY_FILTER_BACKEND: "near-ai"

      # Pinned rather than left to the binary's defaults. Both are MEASURED
      # here, so a contributor who has verified the measurement knows which
      # endpoint and which model this enclave sends prose to, without
      # disassembling the image to read a compiled-in default.
      TRACE_NEAR_AI_PRIVACY_BASE_URL: "https://cloud-api.near.ai/v1"
      TRACE_NEAR_AI_PRIVACY_MODEL: "openai/privacy-filter"

      # Injected encrypted at deploy time and declared in app-compose.json's
      # `allowed_envs`. The NAME is measured; the VALUE is not, and must never
      # be written into this file -- app-compose.json embeds this compose
      # verbatim and is uploaded to the deployer.
      TRACE_NEAR_AI_PRIVACY_API_KEY: ${TRACE_NEAR_AI_PRIVACY_API_KEY:?set at deploy time}

      # 64 MiB. The redacted-envelope cap is 16 MiB and the measured
      # raw-to-envelope ratio on this pilot is about 3.4:1.
      TRACE_COMMONS_WITNESS_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES: "67108864"

      # THE BOUND ON UNAUTHENTICATED WORK. Both routes are unauthenticated, so
      # anyone who can reach `POST /v1/witness` can spend this CVM's cores and,
      # in `full-pipeline`, the NEAR AI capacity billed to the key above. The
      # 64 MiB cap above is per request; it says nothing about how many arrive
      # at once. These two say that.
      #
      # Both are MEASURED, like everything else here: a contributor who has
      # pinned this measurement can verify that the witness they are sending a
      # raw transcript to has a bound at all, and what it is. An operator
      # cannot quietly widen it without moving the measurement.
      #
      # Four at once. #456 established that 8 concurrent classify windows
      # collapse NEAR AI throughput, which is why the filter serialises windows
      # within a request; N concurrent requests put N windows back in flight at
      # the same endpoint, so the bound is set strictly under the 8 that is
      # known to fail. Memory is the other constraint: a request at the 64 MiB
      # cap is buffered, parsed, redacted and re-serialised, so a slot costs a
      # couple of hundred megabytes at the cap.
      TRACE_COMMONS_WITNESS_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS: "4"

      # Five minutes, and the number is measured rather than round. The
      # classifier's largest proven success is a 243 KiB window in 9.3 s, so a
      # request classifies on the order of 25 KiB/s serially: five minutes is
      # several megabytes of transcript. It is also above the ~2 minutes a
      # single window can legitimately take when it retries against the 30 s
      # per-call timeout, so a healthy slow request is not abandoned.
      #
      # A bound with no deadline is not a bound: one request whose classifier
      # call never returns would hold its slot for the life of the process, and
      # four of those would wedge the witness at full occupancy with nothing
      # running. A timed-out request is refused with 504 and its slot is
      # released.
      TRACE_COMMONS_WITNESS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS: "300"

      # Path prefixes the deterministic pass treats as known, so they are not
      # reported as findings. Empty reports more, never less.
      TRACE_COMMONS_WITNESS_KNOWN_PATH_PREFIXES: ""

      # `info` is what the witness logs at, and what it logs is two lines at
      # boot: the signing address and the measurement. Both are public values
      # an operator pins. Do not raise this to `debug` on a deployment that
      # sees real transcripts.
      RUST_LOG: "info"

    ports:
      - "8088:8088"
name: trace-commons-witness
